problems.title: Entropy change of heated water
problems.scenario:
**10 kg** of liquid water is heated from **20 °C** to **80 °C**. Take $c = 4.18\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$.

Find the **entropy change** of the water, in kJ/K.
hints: For an incompressible substance, $\Delta S = m\,c\,\ln(T_2/T_1)$.
problems.solution:
Water is incompressible, so its entropy change depends only on the temperature ratio:

$$\Delta S = m\,c\,\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} = 10 \times 4.18 \times \ln\frac{353}{293}$$

$$\Delta S = 41.8 \times \ln(1.2048) = 41.8 \times 0.1864 = 7.79\ \text{kJ/K}$$

The logarithm needs **absolute** temperatures — a ratio of °C values would be wrong.

problems.title: Isentropic temperature rise
problems.scenario:
Air at **300 K** and **100 kPa** is compressed **isentropically** to **600 kPa**. Take $k = 1.4$.

Find the **exit temperature**, in K.
hints: Use the isentropic $T$–$P$ relation for an ideal gas.
problems.solution:
For an isentropic process with constant specific heats:

$$T_2 = T_1\left(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\right)^{(k-1)/k} = 300\left(\frac{600}{100}\right)^{0.4/1.4}$$

$$T_2 = 300 \times 6^{0.2857} = 300 \times 1.6685 = 500.6\ \text{K}$$

Compressing a gas isentropically always raises its temperature.

problems.title: Entropy change of air (T, P known)
problems.scenario:
Air changes from **300 K, 100 kPa** to **500 K, 500 kPa**. Take $c_p = 1.005$ and $R = 0.287\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$.

Find the **specific entropy change** $\Delta s$, in kJ/(kg·K).
hints: With temperature and pressure given, use the $(T,P)$ form.
The pressure term is *subtracted* — rising pressure lowers entropy.
problems.solution:
Choose the entropy form that matches the given data ($T$ and $P$):

$$\Delta s = c_p\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} - R\ln\frac{P_2}{P_1}$$

Evaluate each term:

$$c_p\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} = 1.005\ln\frac{500}{300} = 1.005 \times 0.5108 = 0.5134$$

$$R\ln\frac{P_2}{P_1} = 0.287\ln 5 = 0.287 \times 1.6094 = 0.4619$$

$$\Delta s = 0.5134 - 0.4619 = 0.0515\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$$

The heating raises entropy while the compression lowers it; here the net is slightly positive.

problems.title: Isentropic expansion (volume ratio)
problems.scenario:
Air at **800 K** expands isentropically until its volume is **8 times** larger ($v_2/v_1 = 8$). Take $k = 1.4$.

Find the **final temperature**, in K.
hints: Note the volume ratio is inverted ($v_1/v_2 = 1/8$).
problems.solution:
For an isentropic process the temperature–volume relation is:

$$T_2 = T_1\left(\frac{v_1}{v_2}\right)^{k-1} = 800\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{0.4}$$

$$T_2 = 800 \times (0.125)^{0.4} = 800 \times 0.4353 = 348.2\ \text{K}$$

Expanding a gas isentropically cools it — the basis of how a turbine drops temperature.

problems.title: Entropy generation in heat transfer
problems.scenario:
**500 kJ** of heat is transferred directly from a source at **800 K** to a sink at **300 K**.

Find the total **entropy generated**, in kJ/K.
hints: Each reservoir changes entropy by $Q/T$: the sink gains $+Q/T_L$, the source loses $-Q/T_H$.
problems.solution:
Heat leaves the source (entropy $-Q/T_H$) and enters the sink (entropy $+Q/T_L$). The total entropy change of everything is the generation:

$$S_{gen} = \frac{Q}{T_L} - \frac{Q}{T_H} = \frac{500}{300} - \frac{500}{800}$$

$$S_{gen} = 1.6667 - 0.625 = 1.042\ \text{kJ/K}$$

It's positive, as the second law demands — heat flowing across a finite temperature difference is irreversible and *generates* entropy.

problems.title: Turbine isentropic efficiency
problems.scenario:
Steam enters a turbine at $h_1 = 3231\ \text{kJ/kg}$. For an isentropic expansion to the exit pressure, the exit enthalpy would be $h_{2s} = 2200\ \text{kJ/kg}$. The turbine's isentropic efficiency is **0.85**.

Find the **actual work output** per kg, in kJ/kg.
hints: Isentropic (ideal) work is the enthalpy drop to $h_{2s}$: $w_s = h_1 - h_{2s}$.
Turbine efficiency = actual work ÷ ideal work, so $w_{act} = \eta_T (h_1 - h_{2s})$.
problems.solution:
The ideal (isentropic) work is the full enthalpy drop to $h_{2s}$:

$$w_s = h_1 - h_{2s} = 3231 - 2200 = 1031\ \text{kJ/kg}$$

The real turbine delivers a fraction $\eta_T$ of that:

$$w_{act} = \eta_T\,(h_1 - h_{2s}) = 0.85 \times 1031 = 876.4\ \text{kJ/kg}$$

Irreversibilities mean the actual exit enthalpy is higher (less work extracted) than the ideal case.

problems.title: Compressor isentropic efficiency
problems.scenario:
Air enters a compressor at $h_1 = 300.19\ \text{kJ/kg}$. The isentropic (ideal) exit enthalpy is $h_{2s} = 430.0\ \text{kJ/kg}$. The compressor's isentropic efficiency is **0.80**.

Find the **actual work input** per kg, in kJ/kg.
hints: For a compressor the efficiency ratio is *inverted* vs a turbine: $\eta_C = w_s/w_{act}$.
problems.solution:
For a compressor, the *ideal* (isentropic) work is the smaller one, so efficiency is ideal ÷ actual:

$$\eta_C = \frac{h_{2s} - h_1}{h_2 - h_1} = \frac{w_s}{w_{act}} \quad\Rightarrow\quad w_{act} = \frac{h_{2s} - h_1}{\eta_C}$$

The ideal work:

$$w_s = h_{2s} - h_1 = 430.0 - 300.19 = 129.81\ \text{kJ/kg}$$

So the actual input is larger:

$$w_{act} = \frac{129.81}{0.80} = 162.3\ \text{kJ/kg}$$

Note the efficiency ratio flips between turbines (actual/ideal) and compressors (ideal/actual) — getting this backwards is a classic mistake.

problems.title: Entropy generated by mixing water
problems.scenario:
**2 kg** of water at **80 °C** is mixed with **2 kg** of water at **20 °C** in an insulated container. Take $c = 4.18\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$.

Find the **entropy generated** by the mixing, in kJ/K.
hints: Equal masses, same fluid → equilibrium temperature is the average: $T_{eq} = (353 + 293)/2 = 323\ \text{K}$.
Each stream's entropy change is $m c \ln(T_{eq}/T_i)$; sum them.
problems.solution:
**Step 1 — equilibrium temperature.** Equal masses of the same fluid average out:

$$T_{eq} = \frac{T_1 + T_2}{2} = \frac{353 + 293}{2} = 323\ \text{K}$$

**Step 2 — entropy change of each stream**, summed (insulated → no entropy transfer, so the total *is* the generation):

$$S_{gen} = m c\ln\frac{T_{eq}}{T_1} + m c\ln\frac{T_{eq}}{T_2}$$

$$S_{gen} = 2(4.18)\left[\ln\frac{323}{353} + \ln\frac{323}{293}\right] = 8.36\,[-0.0888 + 0.0975]$$

$$S_{gen} = 8.36 \times 0.00869 = 0.073\ \text{kJ/K}$$

The hot stream *loses* entropy and the cold one *gains* more, so the total is positive — mixing is irreversible.

problems.title: Real turbine work via isentropic efficiency
problems.scenario:
Air expands through an **adiabatic turbine** from **700 kPa, 750 K** to **100 kPa**, with an isentropic efficiency of **0.88**. Take $c_p = 1.005$, $R = 0.287\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$, $k = 1.4$.

Find the **actual specific work output**, in kJ/kg.
problems.solution:
**Step 1 — isentropic exit temperature** $((k-1)/k = 0.2857)$:

$$T_{2s} = 750\left(\frac{100}{700}\right)^{0.2857} = 750 \times 0.5735 = 430.1\ \text{K}$$

**Step 2 — ideal (isentropic) work:**

$$w_s = c_p(T_1 - T_{2s}) = 1.005(750 - 430.1) = 321.5\ \text{kJ/kg}$$

**Step 3 — actual work** via the isentropic efficiency:

$$w = \eta_T\, w_s = 0.88 \times 321.5 = 283\ \text{kJ/kg}$$
